data.value: Use an original, unencrypted export from the source app. Encrypted Aegis and 2FAS exports are rejected. The following minimal structures show the required fields:

data.name: FaqImportFormatsOtpAuthDescription
data.value: Create a UTF-8 text file with one standard otpauth://totp URI per line. Blank lines and lines beginning with # are ignored. Every URI must contain a non-empty label and a valid Base32 secret and use supported SHA-1, six-digit TOTP parameters. An issuer is recommended; when absent, OTP Harbor uses the label as the issuer.

data.name: FaqMasterPasswordRecoveryQuestion
data.value: Why do I need to keep my master password?

data.name: FaqMasterPasswordRecoveryAnswer
data.value: Your master password protects your vault and remains your recovery method on every supported system, even when you use device authentication. Keep it in a safe place; OTP Harbor cannot reset it.

data.name: FaqOlderVaultsQuestion
data.value: Can I import a vault from an older version of OTP Harbor?

data.name: FaqOlderVaultsAnswer
data.value: Yes, if you have a supported export or backup. In Settings → Data & backup → Import accounts, select the file from the older version. OTP Harbor supports its account exports, password-protected .totp and .otphbp backups, and automatic .otphbackup snapshots. For an encrypted backup, enter the password used when it was created. Keep the original files until you have checked the imported accounts. If the file is unsupported, open it in the older app and export the accounts in a supported format first.

data.name: FaqCreateBackupQuestion
data.value: How do I create a backup?

data.name: FaqCreateBackupAnswer
data.value:
Open Settings → Data & backup. For a manual backup, export your accounts, set and confirm an export password, and choose where to save the encrypted file. Keep this password safe: you need it to import that backup.
For automatic backups, set up a destination folder under Automatic backups and grant access if prompted. OTP Harbor saves encrypted recovery copies when your vault changes. Check the backup status and keep the destination accessible. To restore an automatic copy, you need the master password that was in use when that copy was created.
Keep an additional recovery copy in a separate safe location, and check that you can import a backup before relying on it.
